title: Server Components vs Client Components
description: Distinguish Server Components from Client Components, understand their trade-offs, and learn when to opt into client rendering.

data.text: React Server Components (RSC) change where components run. Server Components execute only on the server, have zero client-side JavaScript footprint, and can read databases or files directly. Client Components run in the browser, manage interactivity, and use hooks. In the App Router model, components are Server Components by default and opt into client rendering with `'use client'`.

Server Components run exclusively on the server. Their result is serialized to a special format and streamed to the client. Because they never execute in the browser, they can access backend resources directly without API routes.

items: Can import server-only libraries like database clients or filesystem APIs
Add zero JavaScript to the client bundle
Can be async and await data directly

data.title: A Server Component fetching data directly
data.content: No API route needed — the component reads the database on the server and streams the HTML.

data.text: Client Components run in the browser. They handle interactivity, local state, effects, and browser APIs. Once you mark a file with `'use client'`, that component and everything it imports become part of the client bundle.

items: Can use useState, useEffect, useContext, and event handlers
Can access window, document, and localStorage

data.title: A Client Component handling interactivity
data.content: Only components that need interactivity should carry the 'use client' directive.

cards.title: Server Components
cards.description: Default component type in the App Router. Runs on the server and streams JSON to the client.

cards.title: Client Components
cards.description: Opt-in components that run in the browser. Required for interactivity and browser APIs.

data.text: You can compose both types by passing Server Component output as props or children to Client Components. The boundary between them is the `'use client'` boundary: anything below it is client-rendered.

data.title: Push Server Components as deep as possible
data.text: Only mark leaf components as Client Components. Keep layouts, data fetching, and markdown rendering on the server. Smaller client boundaries mean smaller bundles and faster hydration.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Server Components are the default in the App Router
Client Components need 'use client' and run in the browser
Minimize client boundaries to reduce bundle size
Pass data from Server to Client Components via props
data.takeaway: A well-structured app has server-rendered shells with small, interactive Client Component leaves.
